_doc: How a bill dies in each state, sourced. Status must never be COMPUTED from these rules — they exist so a human can see when a non-terminal status has become implausible, and so status_basis can be stated honestly.

2025-2026.carryover: First year to second year, by resolution ('reintroduced and retained in present status').
2025-2026.expiration: Unpassed bills die at sine die of the second-year session.
2025-2026.note: Washington records no death action; the page continues to show the last committee location. Absence of a terminal action is NOT evidence of life. This is the rule we misread.

2025-2026.expiration: Unpassed bills fail at the end of the final floor period.
2025-2026.terminal_action_text: Failed to pass pursuant to Senate Joint Resolution 1
2025-2026.note: Wisconsin posts an explicit failure line, so status is evidenced by action, not inferred from the calendar.

2025.carryover: None. Bills die at adjournment and must be refiled.
2025.expiration: Unpassed bills die at adjournment sine die.
2025.note: Missouri records no death action; a bill simply stops. HB 1462's last action was a committee referral on 15 May 2025, the penultimate day.
